outcomes: Trace an ordered feature vector into one prediction
Implement every weight and bias derivative
Fit and reuse training-only scaling statistics
lessons: Why do equal sensor readings need different answers?
How do several measurements become one prediction?
Can one error update every relevant weight?
Why can the unit of load break a correct update?
Can you change units without changing the answer?
What can an extra feature represent, and what can it not?

vector.name: Vector
vector.definition: An ordered collection of numbers treated as one mathematical object.
vector.explanation: A feature vector stores several measurements in a fixed order. Here positions mean raw sensor, load and vibration. A weight vector uses that same schema. Its dot product with one feature vector produces one scalar before bias is added. Fixed arrays enforce the number of entries, but cannot detect a swapped meaning or mismatched units.

dot-product.name: Dot product
dot-product.definition: The sum of products of corresponding entries in two equal-length vectors.
dot-product.explanation: For weights w and features x, their dot product is w₁x₁ + w₂x₂ + and so on. It converts two vectors of the same dimension into one scalar weighted sum. Adding a bias produces a multifeature affine prediction. The order and length must agree. A dot product is not elementwise output: the individual products are reduced by addition. This compact operation will reappear inside every dense neural-network layer.

linear-regression.name: Linear regression
linear-regression.definition: A model that predicts a numeric target from a weighted sum of features.
linear-regression.explanation: Linear regression chooses one coefficient per feature plus an intercept, usually by minimizing squared error. The model is linear in its parameters even when preprocessing transforms the raw features. Coefficients describe changes only under the chosen units and with other features held fixed; correlated features can make causal interpretations unsafe. Here gradient descent fits the coefficients so learners can reuse Chapter 2's machinery, though other solvers can fit the same objective.

feature-scaling.name: Feature scaling
feature-scaling.definition: Transforming feature values to comparable numerical ranges using training statistics.
feature-scaling.explanation: Standardization subtracts each feature's training mean and divides by its training standard deviation. This gives centered, similarly scaled coordinates, so one learning rate can move different weights sensibly. The statistics are fitted on training data and then reused unchanged for validation, test, and inference. Recomputing them on held-out examples leaks information. Scaling affects optimization and coefficient units; it does not create information that the original measurements lacked.

checks: Learner baseline reaches MSE10; complete vector model fits the exact fixture
All four gradient components agree with central differences at a nonzero model
Constant features and invalid data are rejected; standardized feature sums are near zero
limitations: Fixed arrays check dimensions but not semantic feature order
Scaling improves coordinates without creating missing information
Linear coefficients do not establish causation and an additive model misses interactions
